target.title: refactor(agents): converge CLI tool terminal reason onto run-termination
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The one-shot and live CLI runners each derived the same terminal decision — `timed_out` / `cancelled` / `failed` for tools when a run ends — with different logic:

- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.ts` (one-shot) read the abort signal's lifecycle fields, then only recognized `FailoverError` timeouts; a `TimeoutError`-shaped or `AbortError`-shaped run error without an aborted signal classified as `failed`.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.ts` (live) only sniffed error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) and never consulted the abort signal.

Because the live path trusted the delivered error's name alone, a run timeout whose abort reason reached the turn as a generic `AbortError` (or a non-`Error` timeout reason, which `createAbortError` cannot preserve) was reported as `cancelled` instead of `timed_out`; conversely a user cancel racing a timeout-shaped provider error reported `timed_out` where the one-shot path reports `cancelled`. Same decision, two encodings, observable drift — seam 3 of #104219.

## Why This Change Was Made

Converge the derivation onto one owner, per the #104219 change shape. `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` lives in `src/agents/run-termination.ts` — the module that already owns abort→stop-reason semantics (`resolveAgentRunAbortLifecycleFields`) — and encodes one rule: abort-signal lifecycle fields are authoritative when the signal has aborted; error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) classifies otherwise. Both call-site derivations are deleted in the same change; the live turn now carries the run's real abort signal (`ClaudeLiveTurn.abortSignal`, threaded in `createTurn`).

`terminalReason` feeds diagnostic events only (`tool.execution.error` category/reason fields), so behavior changes are contained to diagnostics classification. The per-site `errorCategory` vocabularies (`timeout/aborted/error` vs `aborted/cli_tool_incomplete/cli_tool`) intentionally differ per event source and stay site-local.

## User Impact

Tool-failure diagnostics now classify consistently across CLI runner modes:

- Live runs that hit the run timeout report `timed_out` (previously `cancelled` when the abort reason arrived as a generic `AbortError` or a non-`Error` reason).
- A user cancel racing a timeout-shaped error consistently reports `cancelled` on both paths (signal wins).
- One-shot runs with a `TimeoutError`/`AbortError`-shaped run error and no aborted signal now report `timed_out`/`cancelled` instead of `failed`.

No control-flow, retry, or delivery behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Drift sites and trace: old derivations at `execute.ts` (`resolveToolTerminalReason`) and `claude-live-session.ts` (`failActiveClaudeLiveTools`); live abort delivery via `createAbortError(signal.reason)` loses timeout identity for generic/non-`Error` reasons.
- Tests: table-driven matrix for `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` in `src/agents/run-termination.test.ts` (11 cases), including both drift regressions: "timeout abort wins over generic AbortError" and "cancel abort wins over timeout-shaped error".
- Local: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:import-cycles` all exit 0; focused vitest green (`run-termination`, cli-runner suites — 270+ tests).
- Remote (Blacksmith Testbox, leases `tbx_01kx80mneqrn7dyntk6cjptc4t`, `tbx_01kx837g6z39m9kjrfkr8mvsm8`), branch rebased on latest `main`: `pnpm check:changed` exit 0. `pnpm test:changed` hit two known-flaky failures under full parallel shard load (`model-fallback.probe.test.ts` async log-capture assertion; `Worker exited unexpectedly` on the gateway shard); both pass in isolation on the same lease and diff — probe test 20/20 twice, full gateway shard 402 files / 6454 tests green. Neither touches this diff's surface.
- `git diff --numstat`: +43/−17 prod, +96 tests. Net prod +26 buys the single owner: both call-site derivations deleted, one closed union exported.

### Real behavior proof (ephemeral runtime)

Real `executePreparedCliRun` flow — production executor, real process supervisor spawning a real child process, real `claude-stream-json` parser — with a stub CLI backend (one JSONL `mcp_tool_use` line, then silence; no network, no API keys, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`). Events observed on the trusted tool-execution bus (`onTrustedToolExecutionEvent`; the public `onDiagnosticEvent` filters trusted events). One-shot path exercised; the live session consumes the same shared helper.

Timeout run (no-output watchdog → `FailoverError reason:"timeout"`), redacted:

```json
{
  "type": "tool.execution.error",
  "runId": "run-proof-timeout",
  "toolName": "mcp__openclaw__cron",
  "toolOwner": "cli-runner",
  "toolCallId": "call-proof-timeout",
  "durationMs": 1509,
  "errorCategory": "cli_tool_incomplete",
  "terminalReason": "timed_out"
}
```

User-cancel run (`abortController.abort()` after `tool.execution.started` → `AbortError` with aborted signal), redacted:

```json
{
  "type": "tool.execution.error",
  "runId": "run-proof-cancel",
  "toolName": "mcp__openclaw__cron",
  "toolOwner": "cli-runner",
  "toolCallId": "call-proof-cancel",
  "durationMs": 137,
  "errorCategory": "aborted",
  "terminalReason": "cancelled"
}
```

Branch rebased on current `main` before this update; focused tests + `tsgo:core` green post-rebase.

Part of #104219 (seam 3: CLI-runner terminal reason derivation).

target.title: fix(discord): add timeouts to PluralKit lookup requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord PluralKit lookups are optional inbound message enrichment, but the PluralKit fetch and response body read did not have a deadline. A slow third-party API response could hold Discord message preflight open instead of degrading cleanly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a small PluralKit lookup timeout, preserve the caller abort signal from preflight, and keep the timer active until the API body has been read. Existing 404 handling, bounded error body reads, auth headers, and optional enrichment semantics are unchanged.

The latest head also replaces the Discord-local timeout/abort helper with the shared SDK `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` helper, so PluralKit uses the same timeout diagnostics, safe timer bounds, parent abort relay, and cleanup contract as the rest of the plugin SDK HTTP timeout paths.

## User Impact

If PluralKit is slow or hangs, Discord inbound message handling can abort the optional lookup instead of waiting indefinitely, keeping the core message flow responsive.

## Evidence

Exact head after ordinary branch update: `ab842be7a31b8ff2f77cec586265c35bde20a265`.

Code/merge update:

- Merged current `upstream/main` into `alix/discord-pluralkit-timeouts` with a normal merge commit; no rebase or force-push.
- Resolved the only merge conflict in `extensions/discord/src/pluralkit.ts`.
- Removed the local `createPluralKitLookupSignal` helper.
- PluralKit now calls `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/extension-shared` with `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? 10_000`, `operation: "discord.pluralkit.lookup"`, and the redaction-safe PluralKit URL.
- Cleanup remains in `finally`, so the deadline covers the fetch, non-OK bounded error-body reads, and successful JSON body reads.

Focused validation run in this worktree:

```text
-> passed
```

- Started a local HTTP server that accepts requests and intentionally stalls either before headers or mid-body.
- Called production `resolveDiscordPreflightPluralKitInfo()` with PluralKit enabled.
- The helper loaded the production PluralKit runtime through `loadPluralKitRuntime()`.
- `fetchPluralKitMessageInfo()` used `globalThis.fetch`, wrapped by `resolveFetch()`, and the new SDK `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` path.
- `globalThis.fetch` was temporarily routed from the PluralKit URL to the local stalled server so the network request, abort signal, body read, timeout, catch, and preflight `null` degradation path all ran in-process without Discord credentials.

target.title: fix(secrets): register secret targets for installed-origin plugins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#104320 (P1, regression of #82621/#82798): the secret target registry built its plugin-derived entries from **bundled-origin records only** (`target-registry-data.ts` filtered `record.origin === "bundled"`). When the Exa web providers moved out of bundled origin into an installed plugin package, their config targets (`plugins.entries.exa.config.webSearch.apiKey`) vanished from the gateway's known-target registry — `secrets.resolve` rejects the CLI-discovered target with `unknown target id`, and `infer web search` fails on an unresolved SecretRef before provider I/O, even though the plugin is loaded, enabled, and `secrets audit` reports full resolvability.

## Why This Change Was Made

Per the triage's best-solution shape ("build the known-target registry from active installed-plugin manifest metadata, while preserving plugin enablement, manifest-first laziness, strict allowed-path scoping, and provider-specific ownership"):

- Web-provider and config-contract secret target entries now come from **every active plugin manifest record**, exactly as channel-contract entries already did (they never filtered by origin — the bundled-only filter on the other two families was the inconsistency).
- Scoping is unchanged and stays manifest-owned: an entry is only created for a plugin that declares the web-provider contract **and** marks the config path sensitive in its own manifest hints, or declares the path in `configContracts.secretInputs`. A non-bundled origin cannot widen target paths beyond its own declared contracts, and no plugin runtime is loaded (metadata snapshot only — laziness preserved).
- No hard-coded provider ids, no validation weakening: `isKnownSecretTargetId` remains a closed registry; the registry just covers what's actually installed.

## User Impact

Users of installed (non-bundled) provider plugins with SecretRef-backed credentials — the Exa split being the shipped example — get working `infer web search`/`web fetch` credential resolution again instead of a hard `INVALID_REQUEST` from the gateway.

## Evidence

**Executed real-handler before/after** (the issue's exact `secrets.resolve` params driven through the real `createSecretsHandlers` handler, with an installed-origin Exa manifest record in the metadata snapshot):

| | result |
|---|---|
| current `main` | `ok: false` — `INVALID_REQUEST: invalid secrets.resolve params: unknown target id "plugins.entries.exa.config.webSearch.apiKey"` (byte-identical to the issue's report) |
| this PR | `ok: true` — validation passes, resolution proceeds |

**Regression test** (`target-registry-data.current-snapshot.test.ts`): an installed-origin (`origin: "global"`) record with the web-search contract + sensitive hint + declared secretInput produces the registry entry and `isKnownSecretTargetId` accepts it. **Fails on prior head** with `expected [ 'auth-profiles.api_key.key', …(37) ] to include 'plugins.entries.exa.config.webSearch.apiKey'`.

**Validation:** full `src/secrets` suite **553/553**; `tsgo:core` 0; oxlint/oxfmt clean.

Fixes #104320

target.title: fix(agents): adopt orphaned managed worktrees left by a crash between git worktree add and registry insert
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway crash (OOM kill, forced restart) landing between `git worktree add` and the registry insert inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves an on-disk worktree and an `openclaw/<name>` branch that no managed API can ever see, repair, or remove: `list()`/`get()` never show it, every `gc()` pass skips it forever, and any later `create()` with the same name fails hard with `branch already exists`. The only way out today is manual operator surgery (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) outside the managed API. Reported with source-level analysis in #103239; this PR makes the orphan self-heal (gc adopts it; a retried create adopts it and preserves the caller's owner) while leaving foreign/detached worktrees untouched.

## Summary

- Problem: A crash between `git worktree add` and `insertRegistryWorktree()` inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves a live git worktree + `openclaw/<name>` branch with no registry row. `reconcileOrphans()` explicitly skips it forever (invisible to `list()`/`gc()`), and a retried `create()` with the same name dead-ends on `branch already exists`.
- Why it matters: In real deployments (OOM kill, forced restart) the orphan is permanently unrecoverable through the managed API — only manual `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` unblocks the name.
- What changed: recovery happens through the retried `create()` path only. `create()`'s branch-exists guard self-heals the exact crashed-create signature (live worktree at the derived path on exactly `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>`, no registry row) instead of dead-ending: it atomically claims the path in the registry (`insertRegistryWorktreeIfPathFree()`, a single Kysely `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (live row at path)` — no schema change), then re-provisions (`copyIncludedFiles()` + `runSetupScript()`), preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId` and recording the real resolved base. Only the claim holder may provision or destroy the path: a losing adopter provably touches nothing, and a holder whose re-provisioning fails removes the worktree and deletes its own row. Normal (non-adopting) `create()` registration also goes through the same atomic claim, so every new live registry row is uniqueness-enforced. `reconcileOrphans()`/gc remains preserve-only (upstream behavior) — background adoption is deliberately not shipped (see Risks). `git.ts` additively parses the porcelain `branch` field for the adoption signature check.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): gc/`reconcileOrphans()` behavior is upstream's (foreign/detached worktrees and live git-listed worktrees are preserved untouched; only dead debris is deleted); no schema change, no migration, no changes to `remove()`, snapshots, or CLI output.

This is AI-assisted work (Claude conductor + Claude worker/verifier agents, human-operated); every change was gated on tests written first and independently reviewed by a fresh-context model before submission.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #103239
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: `create()` performs the irreversible git-side effects (`git worktree add`, branch creation) before the registry insert, with no crash-window reconciliation: `reconcileOrphans()` treated "git still lists this directory as a live worktree" purely as a preserve signal and never checked whether the worktree matches the managed naming scheme but lacks a registry row.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no adopt-or-repair path for the crashed-create signature; `create()`'s branch-exists guard had no way to distinguish "user's foreign branch" from "our own crashed create()".
- Contributing context (if known): the registry has no `name` column (name derives from the path's last segment), so adoption needs no extra bookkeeping — the orphan is fully re-derivable from path + branch.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [ ] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: a live worktree + managed branch with no registry row (the exact end-state of a crash between `git worktree add` and the registry insert) is adopted by a retried `create()` with the same name — preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId`, re-running provisioning (include files + setup script restored, real `baseRef` recorded), and holding the loser-touches-nothing / holder-only-destruction invariants under deterministic interleavings; gc during an in-flight normal `create()` adopts nothing and exactly one live row remains; a failing setup during adoption-retry leaves no worktree, branch, or registry row.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the tests use the real `git` binary and real SQLite registry (the file's established pattern — no mocks), produce the crash end-state via production code (`create()` then deleting only the registry row), and assert through the public service API only.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): "deletes unregistered orphan debris but preserves git-listed worktrees" covers the foreign/detached case and stays green, locking in that non-managed worktrees are never claimed.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A — two new tests added.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- A retried `create()` with the same name after a crashed create now succeeds (adopts, re-provisions, returns the record) instead of failing with `branch already exists`.
- gc behavior is unchanged from upstream (preserve-only for live worktrees); foreign or detached-HEAD worktrees are unaffected.
- Concurrent same-path registrations can no longer produce duplicate live registry rows (atomic claim; loser gets the existing "name already in use" semantics).

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
create() crash after `git worktree add` -> live worktree + branch, no registry row
  -> create(same name): "branch already exists" (dead end; manual git surgery required)

After:
create() crash after `git worktree add` -> live worktree + branch, no registry row
  -> create(same name): exact orphan signature -> atomic path claim -> re-provision
     (owner + real base preserved) -> returns record
  -> claim loser (concurrent registration won): touches nothing; standard in-use semantics
  -> gc: preserve-only (unchanged upstream behavior)
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A. Adoption is gated on an exact `git worktree list --porcelain` path + `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>` branch match; fabricating that state requires local filesystem/git access equivalent to what `create()` already requires. `insertRegistryWorktree` is the same call path `create()` already uses.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 26 (arm64); fix is platform-independent (pure git + SQLite service logic)
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / bun, source checkout
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): default `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`-backed state

### Steps

1. `ManagedWorktreeService.create({ repoRoot, name: "task-1" })` and kill the process after `git worktree add` completes but before the registry insert (repro: create normally, then delete only the registry row — identical end state).
2. Run `service.create({ repoRoot, name: "task-1" })` again.

### Expected

- retried create succeeds (adopts, re-provisions, returns the record); gc preserves the orphan untouched.

### Actual

- Before this PR: gc skips it forever; retried create throws `branch already exists: openclaw/task-1`. After this PR: expected behavior (see tests).

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Before (tests added, fix stashed):

```
❯ |agents| src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts (24 tests | 2 failed)
FAIL … adopts a worktree orphaned when create() crashed …, during gc()
  AssertionError: expected undefined to match object {…}
FAIL … adopts an orphaned worktree instead of throwing on a retried create() …
  Error: branch already exists: openclaw/orphan-retry
```

After:

```
pnpm test src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/registry.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  36 passed (36)
```

Real-behavior proof (after-fix run through the actual service recovery path, genuine `kill -9` inside the crash window — exit 137 — against a real git repo + real SQLite registry, covering both the retried-create adoption with re-provisioning and the gc registration-only adoption): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103390#issuecomment-4937129438

Also green on the touched surface: `pnpm tsgo:core` (exit 0), `oxlint` (0 findings), `oxfmt --check` (formatted). Note: repo-wide `pnpm check` currently fails in its preflight `npm shrinkwrap guard` on an unmodified `origin/main` checkout in this environment (`ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` for the `defu` override) — pre-existing and unrelated; no lockfile/override files are touched by this PR.

The previously-acknowledged gc-vs-create double-insert race is now eliminated by the atomic path claim (deterministic interleaving tests cover both directions, with a pasted negative control showing the pre-claim code produces the duplicate row). Remaining narrow edge deliberately out of scope: a lingering *removed* registry row at the same path still blocks create()-side adoption for a fresh orphan (name-reuse-after-remove + crash sequence).

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: full scoped test suite (25/25) against real git + real SQLite locally, including both new adoption tests and the pre-existing foreign-worktree preservation test; typecheck/lint/format on the touched files.
- Edge cases checked: detached-HEAD foreign worktree (preserved), bare branch collision without a live worktree (still throws), owner preservation (`workboard`/`ownerId`) on retried-create adoption including `findLiveByOwner()` lookup, crash-before-setup retry re-provisioning (include file + setup marker restored, real base recorded), and full cleanup on a failing setup script during adoption-retry.
- What you did **not** verify: a literal `kill -9` mid-`create()` on a production gateway (the crash end-state is reproduced through the service's own code paths instead); the two out-of-scope narrow edges above.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: crash orphans with auto-generated names (never retried by name) remain unregistered — background adoption is deliberately not shipped, because distinguishing a gc-found crash orphan from a legitimate manual worktree requires a schema-backed recovery marker + migration (maintainer-owned surface); offered as a follow-up.
  - Mitigation: such orphans keep today's preserve-only behavior (never deleted); explicit-name retries — the reported repro — fully recover.
- Risk: adopting a worktree that a user intentionally created outside the managed API at the exact managed path on an `openclaw/<name>` branch.
  - Mitigation: that state is indistinguishable from (and equivalent to) a crashed managed create; adoption only registers it — it never deletes or modifies the worktree.
- Risk: concurrent adoption attempts (gc vs retried create) racing for one path.

Task: req-20260711-openclaw-gpt56-pr

Fixes an issue where users running GPT-5.6 Sol through the OpenClaw Codex runtime could receive Codex's "requires a newer version" error even though OpenClaw manages a newer Codex app-server package.

target.title: fix(memory): rank filename and path matches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`memory_search` indexed only chunk bodies. Exact filename and date-stem queries such as `2026-06-17-1649` could therefore behave like vector-only semantic searches and omit the indexed file whose basename exactly matched the query.

Fixes #94102.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintainer rewrite keeps path retrieval separate from body retrieval instead of prefixing every chunk's FTS payload with its path. A one-row-per-source path FTS index is maintained from the canonical source table and rebuilt transactionally during shadow publication.

Search carries one closed specificity tier (`full path > basename > stem > partial`) through FTS-only and hybrid ranking. Exact identifiers remain ahead of semantic neighbors, while body/vector relevance orders duplicates within the same tier. Unicode normalization, short trigram terms, source scoping, temporal decay, MMR, existing-database backfill, `VACUUM` rowid changes, and duplicate basenames beyond the candidate cap have dedicated regressions.

This design leaves body FTS bytes, BM25 scores, snippets, embeddings, and embedding-cache identity unchanged; existing indexes gain only the derived path table and do not re-embed.

## User Impact

Searching an exact memory path, basename, filename stem, generated timestamp, or partial path now surfaces the intended memory file before unrelated semantic neighbors. Body searches keep their existing ranking and snippets, with no new configuration or reindex requirement.

## Evidence

- Exact pushed head: `670b3e3f1cc302f0908b426704ef6951380f348f`.
- Focused coverage spans path/body search, hybrid/FTS-only ranking, schema startup and mutation triggers, shadow publication, duplicate basenames, Unicode NFC/NFD, CJK, temporal decay, and MMR.
- Targeted `oxfmt` and `git diff --check`: clean.
- Fresh branch-scoped structured autoreview: clean after addressing its duplicate-basename candidate-cap finding.

## DEV-20260711-001

### Bug fix: Guard OpenAI/Codex GPT-5.6 availability boundaries
- Keeps direct OpenAI API GPT-5.6 support intact.
- Keeps successful ChatGPT/Codex OAuth live discovery authoritative, so account-scoped omissions are not overridden with static rows.
- Keeps bare `gpt-5.6` out of Codex OAuth fallback; OAuth fallback remains limited to supported Codex-family rows.
- Adds focused regression coverage for sparse visible discovery and hidden-only discovery fallback.

## What Problem This Solves

PR #104185 attempted to restore GPT-5.6 availability, but its review found two provider-boundary regressions:

- bare `gpt-5.6` was added to the ChatGPT/Codex OAuth path;
- successful sparse Codex discovery was supplemented with local static fallback rows.

That can make OAuth users select models not advertised for their authenticated account and then fail only at invocation. This PR preserves the intended boundary: direct OpenAI API model availability is separate from account-scoped ChatGPT/Codex OAuth discovery.

## Evidence

- Rejection analysis: #104185 ClawSweeper review asked to remove bare `gpt-5.6` from ChatGPT/Codex OAuth resolution and keep successful visible Codex discovery authoritative.
- Source evidence: this PR only changes `extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts` and `extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts`; it does not add `gpt-5.6` to `OPENAI_CODEX_GPT_56_MODEL_IDS` or static OAuth fallback.
- Behavior evidence: the focused regression test `keeps successful sparse Codex catalog rows authoritative` now asserts a successful visible Codex response containing only `gpt-5.4` remains exactly `['gpt-5.4']` and does not append `gpt-5.6`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.5`, or `gpt-5.3-codex-spark`.
- Behavior evidence: hidden-only Codex discovery is covered as a fallback case, preserving the existing static OAuth fallback path only when there are no usable visible live rows.
- Local validation: `git diff --check` passed.
- Local validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-provider-openai.config.ts extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-provider.test.ts --reporter=dot --no-color` passed with 2 test files and 63 tests.
- GitHub validation observed before this body edit: QA Smoke CI, lint, type, package-boundary, dependency/security guard, and changed-path scans passed; the only failing check was `Real behavior proof` due to missing authored `Evidence` section in the PR body.

### Tests

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-provider-openai.config.ts extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-provider.test.ts --reporter=dot --no-color`: pass, 2 files / 63 tests

### Changed files
- `extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts`
- `extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts`

## User Impact

Direct OpenAI API users keep the existing GPT-5.6 model surface. ChatGPT/Codex OAuth users see only the models returned by their successful account-scoped Codex catalog, avoiding picker entries that may not be authorized for invocation.

## Notes

- No dependency, workflow, permission, or secret-handling changes.
- Does not merge or deploy.
- Follow-up/replacement path for #104185.

target.title: refactor(agents): converge CLI tool terminal reason onto run-termination
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The one-shot and live CLI runners each derived the same terminal decision — `timed_out` / `cancelled` / `failed` for tools when a run ends — with different logic:

- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.ts` (one-shot) read the abort signal's lifecycle fields, then only recognized `FailoverError` timeouts; a `TimeoutError`-shaped or `AbortError`-shaped run error without an aborted signal classified as `failed`.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.ts` (live) only sniffed error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) and never consulted the abort signal.

Because the live path trusted the delivered error's name alone, a run timeout whose abort reason reached the turn as a generic `AbortError` (or a non-`Error` timeout reason, which `createAbortError` cannot preserve) was reported as `cancelled` instead of `timed_out`; conversely a user cancel racing a timeout-shaped provider error reported `timed_out` where the one-shot path reports `cancelled`. Same decision, two encodings, observable drift — seam 3 of #104219.

## Why This Change Was Made

Converge the derivation onto one owner, per the #104219 change shape. `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` lives in `src/agents/run-termination.ts` — the module that already owns abort→stop-reason semantics (`resolveAgentRunAbortLifecycleFields`) — and encodes one rule: abort-signal lifecycle fields are authoritative when the signal has aborted; error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) classifies otherwise. Both call-site derivations are deleted in the same change; the live turn now carries the run's real abort signal (`ClaudeLiveTurn.abortSignal`, threaded in `createTurn`).

`terminalReason` feeds diagnostic events only (`tool.execution.error` category/reason fields), so behavior changes are contained to diagnostics classification. The per-site `errorCategory` vocabularies (`timeout/aborted/error` vs `aborted/cli_tool_incomplete/cli_tool`) intentionally differ per event source and stay site-local.

## User Impact

Tool-failure diagnostics now classify consistently across CLI runner modes:

- Live runs that hit the run timeout report `timed_out` (previously `cancelled` when the abort reason arrived as a generic `AbortError` or a non-`Error` reason).
- A user cancel racing a timeout-shaped error consistently reports `cancelled` on both paths (signal wins).
- One-shot runs with a `TimeoutError`/`AbortError`-shaped run error and no aborted signal now report `timed_out`/`cancelled` instead of `failed`.

No control-flow, retry, or delivery behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Drift sites and trace: old derivations at `execute.ts` (`resolveToolTerminalReason`) and `claude-live-session.ts` (`failActiveClaudeLiveTools`); live abort delivery via `createAbortError(signal.reason)` loses timeout identity for generic/non-`Error` reasons.
- Tests: table-driven matrix for `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` in `src/agents/run-termination.test.ts` (11 cases), including both drift regressions: "timeout abort wins over generic AbortError" and "cancel abort wins over timeout-shaped error".
- Local: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:import-cycles` all exit 0; focused vitest green (`run-termination`, cli-runner suites — 270+ tests).
- Remote (Blacksmith Testbox, leases `tbx_01kx80mneqrn7dyntk6cjptc4t`, `tbx_01kx837g6z39m9kjrfkr8mvsm8`), branch rebased on latest `main`: `pnpm check:changed` exit 0. `pnpm test:changed` hit two known-flaky failures under full parallel shard load (`model-fallback.probe.test.ts` async log-capture assertion; `Worker exited unexpectedly` on the gateway shard); both pass in isolation on the same lease and diff — probe test 20/20 twice, full gateway shard 402 files / 6454 tests green. Neither touches this diff's surface.
- `git diff --numstat`: +43/−17 prod, +96 tests. Net prod +26 buys the single owner: both call-site derivations deleted, one closed union exported.

### Real behavior proof (ephemeral runtime)

Real `executePreparedCliRun` flow — production executor, real process supervisor spawning a real child process, real `claude-stream-json` parser — with a stub CLI backend (one JSONL `mcp_tool_use` line, then silence; no network, no API keys, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`). Events observed on the trusted tool-execution bus (`onTrustedToolExecutionEvent`; the public `onDiagnosticEvent` filters trusted events). One-shot path exercised; the live session consumes the same shared helper.

Timeout run (no-output watchdog → `FailoverError reason:"timeout"`), redacted:

```json
{
  "type": "tool.execution.error",
  "runId": "run-proof-timeout",
  "toolName": "mcp__openclaw__cron",
  "toolOwner": "cli-runner",
  "toolCallId": "call-proof-timeout",
  "durationMs": 1509,
  "errorCategory": "cli_tool_incomplete",
  "terminalReason": "timed_out"
}
```

User-cancel run (`abortController.abort()` after `tool.execution.started` → `AbortError` with aborted signal), redacted:

```json
{
  "type": "tool.execution.error",
  "runId": "run-proof-cancel",
  "toolName": "mcp__openclaw__cron",
  "toolOwner": "cli-runner",
  "toolCallId": "call-proof-cancel",
  "durationMs": 137,
  "errorCategory": "aborted",
  "terminalReason": "cancelled"
}
```

Branch rebased on current `main` before this update; focused tests + `tsgo:core` green post-rebase.

Part of #104219 (seam 3: CLI-runner terminal reason derivation).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes web-search credential presence detection so the audit only reports usable web-search credentials after applying plugin policy, selected provider scoping, and provider-specific env/auth contracts.

The earlier detector could treat credentials from blocked plugins or unrelated providers as web-search credentials. The latest fix also handles the Google plugin's split contracts: selecting `gemini` no longer counts `google-vertex` env such as `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` as a Gemini web-search key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Security/audit surfaces should reflect the selected web-search provider's actual runtime credential contract. Plugin manifests can contain multiple providers and env vars, so manifest env scanning must not flatten unrelated provider credentials into one web-search-positive result.

## User Impact

- Disabled, denied, or non-selected web-search plugins no longer make `web_search` look credentialed.
- Missing env-backed SecretRefs fail closed consistently.
- `tools.web.search.provider: "gemini"` with only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` no longer reports Gemini web search as configured.

commands.author: Glucksberg

target.title: feat(skills): preview proposals before approval
target.body:
Closes #103871

## Summary

- add a read-only `review` action to `skill_workshop`
- render create proposals as their complete canonical applied skill and update proposals as unified diffs
- bound previews with line-aware pagination, proposal-version binding, and explicit drift/integrity outcomes
- keep presentation portable so channels can attach “View skill” / “View diff” actions without Skill Workshop policy

## What Problem This Solves

Approval messages currently provide only a prose summary. Operators cannot inspect the exact skill that a create proposal will install or see additions and removals in an update before approving it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The review projection belongs beside Skill Workshop validation and apply semantics, not in Telegram or another transport. The service computes the canonical read-only result; the agent tool owns bounded presentation and pagination.

## User Impact

Existing Proposal-ID-only lifecycle flows remain compatible. New review flows can bind later pages and apply/reject/quarantine decisions to `proposal_version`, preventing a reviewed proposal from silently changing before the decision. Approval requests resolved by skill name now carry the resolved proposal ID as well as its version into execution.

## Evidence

- 239 focused Vitest tests pass on the final rebased commit.
- Production and test tsgo checks pass.
- Exact-file oxlint/oxfmt, docs formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh structured autoreview found and prompted one approval-parameter fix; review of both that fix and the final 115,842-character branch bundle then reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- A redacted, inspectable live Telegram recording covers create/update review, pagination, first-page lifecycle controls, approval/rejection, and stale-version rejection. The direct artifact link is in **Real behavior proof** below.
- The broad remote `pnpm check:changed` lane could not start from this host: the configured Blacksmith client is absent and the AWS fallback broker is not authenticated. GitHub CI remains the broad remote gate.

## Verification

```bash
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts \
  src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.test.ts \
  src/agents/tool-mutation.test.ts \
  src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.embedded-mode.test.ts

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs $(git diff --name-only upstream/main...HEAD -- '*.ts')
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/skills/workshop/policy.ts src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts
pnpm format:docs:check
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main
```

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: preview the exact canonical result of a Skill Workshop proposal before approval and bind the later lifecycle decision to that reviewed version.
Real environment tested: live Telegram DM on the deployed production-patched OpenClaw runtime at `ef2acbbe69b52f92c788188de3b159de92ad24ef`; all 19 files touched by PR head `87a5fbc3b42da0d1e7322a34bcf038e9451b2607` are byte-identical in that runtime.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: review a paginated create proposal and its first-page Approve/Reject/Next controls; revise v1 to v2 and attempt approval from the stale v1 prompt; review and approve the fresh v2 prompt; review an update proposal's unified diff and reject it.
Evidence after fix: [redacted H.264 Telegram recording](https://f005.backblazeb2.com/file/Hetzner-Openclaw/pr-artifacts/openclaw-103872/87a5fbc3/1691a798/pr-103872-telegram-proof.mp4?Authorization=3_20260711090657_c2ed04244ad7b5248a3e644a_2539c27da42238cee21c9519b915add2b4ae651b_005_20260718090657_0075_dnld) (71.37 seconds, 4,480,020 bytes, SHA-256 `1691a798025c9ffa45bd8ffd6b91980079dcf23d069bdc5b598adb6f93727da5`; temporary public link valid through 2026-07-18 09:06 UTC). Timeline: 00:00 create preview/pagination, 00:23 stale-v1 rejection, 00:36 fresh-v2 review/approval, 00:50 update diff/rejection.
Observed result after fix: create approval succeeds only for the reviewed current version; stale approval fails closed with expected-v1/current-v2 feedback; update review shows the unified diff; Approve and Reject remain available from page 1.
What was not tested: a separate burner-account Crabbox run or a runtime whose overall Git commit exactly equals the PR head; the live runtime instead uses a production integration commit whose complete PR-touched source is byte-identical to the final head.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted: yes. Codex implemented the change, ran focused validation, and completed repeated code-review passes. No agent transcript is attached.

target.title: fix(gateway): add per-request cancellation to prevent late node.invoke dispatch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A pending plugin approval can execute dangerous `node.invoke` work after the originating Gateway request has already timed out or disconnected. This is a P1 security vulnerability (fixes #103980): the plugin approval window (120s default) exceeds the Gateway client timeout (30s default), creating a deterministic window where dangerous node commands can dispatch side effects after the caller has already observed failure.

Root cause: The TypeScript Gateway client removes its local waiter on timeout/abort but never signals cancellation to the server. The server-side WebSocket handler launches a detached promise without retaining per-request cancellation state. On persistent WebSocket connections, a client-local timeout does not close the socket, so the server never observes the cancellation boundary.

## Evidence

### Proof test results (18 tests across 3 environments)

```
$ pnpm vitest run src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ PROOF-P2: pre-aborted signal immediately expires approval without waiting (54ms)
 ✓ PROOF-P1: abort during dispatch window is captured by listener guard (2ms)
 ✓ PROOF-P1: pre-aborted signal prevents any node registry invoke call (1ms)
 ✓ PROOF-race: approval cancellation wins when abort fires before decision (2ms)
 ✓ PROOF-normal: approval flow works correctly when no abort occurs (3ms)
 ✓ PROOF-deadline: request-level deadline cancels even without socket close (2ms)

 Test Files  3 passed (3) | Tests  18 passed (18) | Duration 8.56s
```

### Full test suite (57 tests)

```
$ pnpm vitest run src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.proof.test.ts

 Test Files  6 passed (6) | Tests  57 passed (57) | Duration 10.25s
```

### Cancellation matrix

| Input form | Result |
|---|---|
| Approval completes before abort | `decision: "allow-once"` — normal flow |
| Abort fires before approval decision | `decision: null` (expired via `caller-aborted`) |
| Pre-aborted signal before `request()` | `decision: null` (immediate expiry, P2 fix) |
| Abort fires between check and invoke | `REQUEST_CANCELLED` (atomic guard, P1 fix) |
| Pre-aborted signal before `invokeNode()` | `REQUEST_CANCELLED` (no transport call) |
| Request deadline fires (persistent conn) | `decision: null` (deadline cancels even without socket close) |
| Normal flow without abortSignal | Unchanged behavior — backward compatible |

### Key proof: atomic dispatch guard prevents late side effects

The listener guard registers a one-shot `abort` listener that sets `cancelledBeforeDispatch = true` **before** any dispatch. A re-check after registration closes the race window. When the abort fires between the initial check and `nodeRegistry.invoke()`, the guard catches it and **the dangerous command never reaches the transport**:

```typescript
// P1 fix: atomic dispatch guard
let cancelledBeforeDispatch = false;
const onAbort = () => { cancelledBeforeDispatch = true; };
params.abortSignal?.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true });
try {
  if (params.abortSignal?.aborted || cancelledBeforeDispatch) {
    return { ok: false, code: "REQUEST_CANCELLED", ... };
  }
  // ... dispatch ...
} finally {
  params.abortSignal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
}
```

### Key proof: request-level deadline covers persistent connections

On persistent WebSocket connections where a client-local timeout (30s) does NOT close the socket, the server adds a request-level deadline timer using `MAX_PLUGIN_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS`. When this deadline fires, it aborts the per-request controller, expiring any pending approval even though the socket is still alive:

```typescript
// In message-handler.ts:
const requestDeadlineTimer = setTimeout(() => {
  cancelRequest("request-deadline-exceeded");
}, MAX_PLUGIN_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS);
```

### Key proof: pre-abort expiry prevents dangling approvals

AbortSignal does not replay past events. If `abortSignal.aborted` is already `true` when `addEventListener("abort")` is called, the listener never fires. The fix checks `abortSignal.aborted` before registering the listener and immediately expires the approval:

```typescript
// P2 fix: check before listener registration
if (params.abortSignal.aborted) {
  manager.expire(record.id, "caller-aborted");
  return { id: record.id, decision: null };
}
```

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.ts` | Atomic dispatch guard + pre-abort expiry + signal propagation |
| `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.proof.test.ts` | 6 proof tests covering all cancellation scenarios |
| `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts` | 3 new cancellation regression tests |
| `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.ts` | Request-level deadline + cancelRequest() + .finally() cleanup |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/shared-types.ts` | `abortSignal` in `GatewayRequestHandlerOptions` |
| `src/gateway/server-methods.ts` | Forward `abortSignal` to handler invocation |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts` | Pass `abortSignal` to `applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy` |

---

## Summary

**Updated to address ClawSweeper review findings (Round 3):**
- ✅ [P1] Make cancellation atomic with node dispatch — abort listener guard + re-check after registration
- ✅ [P2] Check for already-aborted signal before awaiting approval — immediate expiry on pre-abort
- ✅ [P1] Cancel timed-out requests, not only closed sockets — request-level deadline timer
- ✅ [P1] Preserve request dispatch error handling — removed empty catch
- ✅ Forward `abortSignal` through `handleGatewayRequest` → `GatewayRequestHandlerOptions` → handler invocation
- ✅ Pass `abortSignal` from `node.invoke` handler to `applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy` to `createApprovalRuntime`
- ✅ Add `.finally()` cleanup for per-request socket close listener
- ✅ Add 6 proof tests + 3 regression tests

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API /contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Fixes #103980
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — abortSignal is optional parameter
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Diagram

```
Before fix:
Client --timeout--> removes local waiter
Server ---------------> awaits approval (120s) -----> allows -----> node.invoke executes ❌

After fix:
Client --timeout/abort/close--> fires AbortSignal
Server --sees abort--> expires approval -----> blocks node.invoke ✅
Signal flow: WebSocket → handleGatewayRequest → node.invoke handler → applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy
             └→ createApprovalRuntime (pre-abort check)
             └→ invokeNode (atomic guard: check → listener → re-check → dispatch)
```

---

Fixes #103980

target.title: fix(discord): keep voice diagnostics bounded when ffmpeg errors are multibyte

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users playing Discord voice audio could receive ffmpeg failure diagnostics that exceed the existing 8,192-byte cap when ffmpeg emits multibyte stderr text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord voice playback boundary now retains stderr as bytes and decodes the retained prefix safely after ffmpeg exits. This keeps the existing diagnostic cap accurate without changing playback, configuration, or channel behavior.

## User Impact

Discord voice playback failures keep a bounded, readable ffmpeg diagnostic even when the underlying error text contains multibyte characters.

## Evidence

- Current head: `71fc6655daae1a2496fbc49159ecc544086222b6`.

target.title: fix(feishu): add 30 s request timeout to streaming-card API calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where all six outbound CardKit and tenant-token requests in
`extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts` called `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without
a `timeoutMs` deadline. If the Feishu API endpoint accepts a TCP connection but
never completes the HTTP response (stalled server, network middlebox, proxy delay),
the affected call blocks indefinitely and pins a gateway request lane open.

The critical path is `getToken()`: tenant-token refresh is called before every
CardKit request, so a single stalled token endpoint blocks the entire streaming-card
reply pipeline for a running agent turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` exposes a top-level `timeoutMs` parameter that applies a hard
abort deadline to the underlying request. Adding `FEISHU_STREAMING_CARD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`
and wiring it to all six call sites in one constant covers every streaming-card path
without touching callers.

The 30-second value matches the sibling pattern already used across the codebase
(e.g. `extensions/googlechat/src/api.ts`, `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts`,
`extensions/mattermost/src/api.ts`).

`extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts` was checked and is not affected: its
`fetchFeishuJson` helper receives `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS)`
through the caller's `init`, providing equivalent protection via a different mechanism.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled Feishu API endpoint leaves tenant-token refresh or any CardKit
request pending indefinitely. No timeout error is surfaced; the streaming-card reply
lane is blocked until the process is restarted.

**After:** Every streaming-card API request fails with an abort/timeout error after
30 seconds. The caller receives a concrete error, the lane is released, and the gateway
can continue processing other messages.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/feishu-streaming-card-timeouts`  
Base: `upstream/main`  
Node: v22.22.0 — macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64

### Existing tests — all passing after change

```
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > reports no visible content when final close update fails before any accepted text
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > bounds streaming token cache lifetime when token expiry overflows
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > bounds streaming token fallback lifetime when the process clock is invalid
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > treats an invalid process clock as a streaming token cache miss
 ... (7 more)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

target.title: fix(agents): keep bundle LSP tool names provider-safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users enabling bundled LSP servers with human-readable server keys could expose invalid or colliding agent tool names when those keys contain spaces, punctuation, numeric prefixes, or overlap with an existing registered tool name.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundle LSP runtime now keeps the original server key for user-facing labels and execution details while deriving a provider-safe model-facing tool prefix for hover, definition, and references tools. The prefix is bounded to the existing 64-character tool-name budget and disambiguated against sibling LSP prefixes plus already registered tool names, matching the bundle MCP naming boundary without changing configuration, provider routing, or LSP protocol behavior.

## User Impact

Agents can use bundled LSP hover, definition, and references tools for readable server names such as `Type Script!` or numeric keys, and LSP tools are no longer dropped when the sanitized name would collide with a registered tool.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(agents): honor Anthropic Retry-After in auto-retry backoff (#103849)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the default Anthropic Messages transport (used by `anthropic-messages` models), a 429 response carrying a server-specified `Retry-After` header lost its HTTP status and cooldown metadata before the agent retry/failover owner saw it. The embedded runner could therefore retry or rotate profiles inside a still-active provider cooldown, including shortening a provider-requested 120-second window to the normal first auth-profile cooldown.

Closes #103849

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed transport already parses provider HTTP responses, but the thrown error did not preserve `httpStatus` / `retryAfterSeconds` through `extractTransportErrorDetails` into `AssistantMessage`. OpenClaw's supported embedded-runner path also disables `AgentSession` auto-retry and owns retry/failover in `run.ts`, so the server cooldown has to reach the embedded runner and auth-profile cooldown state, not only the session inner loop.

## Changes

- `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts` attaches structured HTTP status and canonical Retry-After parsing to non-OK Anthropic Messages errors.
- `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts` preserves `httpStatus` and `retryAfterSeconds`, including overflow `Infinity`, on assistant errors.
- `packages/llm-core/src/types.ts` adds optional `AssistantMessage.httpStatus` / `retryAfterSeconds` metadata.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/assistant-failover.ts` routes short Retry-After windows into same-model rate-limit retry and routes over-limit windows into auth-profile failure marking.
- `src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts` keeps rate-limited profiles unavailable for at least the server Retry-After window while preserving existing `cooldownReason`, `cooldownModel`, and failure-count semantics.
- `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts` keeps the same structured metadata usable for the non-default session auto-retry path without making it the supported OpenClaw retry owner.

## User Impact

Anthropic 429s with a short Retry-After now wait out the provider's cooldown before retrying the same model. Longer provider cooldowns no longer collapse to the default 30-second profile cooldown; the profile stays unavailable for the server-requested window and the runner proceeds through the existing fallback/rotation path instead of hammering a still-rate-limited profile.

## Evidence

Current head: `cc968b5a6a`.

Red/green proof for the latest review finding:
- Before the fix, `markAuthProfileFailure(... retryAfterSeconds: 120)` produced `cooldownUntil = now + 30_000`; after the fix it produces `now + 120_000`.
- Before the fix, embedded failover marked the failed profile without `retryAfterSeconds`; after the fix it passes `retryAfterSeconds: 120` into auth-profile failure marking.

Focused current-head proof:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/assistant-failover.test.ts -t "Retry-After"` -> 12 passed / 58 skipped
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.test.ts -t "per-model cooldown metadata"` -> 14 passed / 146 skipped
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts -t "structured Retry-After"` -> 4 passed / 236 skipped
- `cmd /c node_modules\.bin\oxfmt --check --threads=1 ...touched files...` -> pass
- `git diff --check` -> pass

Earlier transport/parser proof on this PR:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/transport-stream-shared.test.ts -t "propagates httpStatus"` -> 2 passed / 24 skipped
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts -t "surfaces HTTP status and Retry-After"` -> 2 passed / 216 skipped
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts -t "over-limit Retry-After"` -> 2 passed / 216 skipped
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/provider-transport-fetch.test.ts -t "retry-after"` -> 58 passed / 134 skipped
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/retry.auto-retry-delay.test.ts -t "server Retry-After"` -> 4 passed / 3 skipped

target.title: fix(agents): respect provider default thinking level over global thinkingDefault
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron agentTurn jobs using Ollama models produce empty responses when `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` is configured, because the global default unconditionally overrides the provider's own default of `"off"`.

- **Problem**: `resolveThinkingDefault()` checks `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` before the provider-specific default, so when a user has `thinkingDefault: "low"` (common for Claude), Ollama receives a non-`"off"` thinking level → `think: true` in the Ollama API → model consumes 100% of output tokens on reasoning → empty `content` → "Agent couldn't generate a response"
- **Solution**: Resolve the provider-specific default first, then only apply the global `thinkingDefault` when the provider does not explicitly default to `"off"`
- **What changed**: `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts` (reorder evaluation in `resolveThinkingDefault()`), new test file `src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts`
- **What did NOT change**: Per-model `params.thinking` priority, Claude hardcoded special cases, the Ollama provider plugin, or any behavior for providers without an explicit default

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #104212

- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` is set to enable thinking for the primary model (usually Claude), the global default unconditionally overrides every provider's own default thinking level. For Ollama, which explicitly defaults to `"off"` in `extensions/ollama/provider-policy-api.ts`, this forces `think: true` in the Ollama API request, causing models like Qwen3.5-4B to consume all output tokens on reasoning and produce zero visible content.

The same Ollama workflow works correctly when no global `thinkingDefault` is set, or when `params.thinking` is explicitly configured per model.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Global `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` must not override provider-specific defaults that are `"off"`
- Real environment tested: Ubuntu Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/ollama-respect-default-thinking-104212`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
pnpm tsgo:core      # type check
npx oxfmt --check src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts  # format check
npx oxlint --deny-warnings src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts  # lint check
pnpm test src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts --run  # unit tests
pnpm check:import-cycles  # cycle check
```

- Evidence after fix (real runtime invocation via `resolveThinkingDefault()`):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "import { resolveThinkingDefault } from './src/agents/model-thinking-default.js'; ..."

Real Behavior Evidence — PR #104248 / Fixes #104212
Environment: Node v22.19.0, linux
========================================
PASS | Ollama + global thinkingDefault=low                     result=off (expected off)
PASS | Ollama + global thinkingDefault=adaptive                result=off (expected off)
PASS | Ollama + global thinkingDefault=off                     result=off (expected off)
PASS | No global default                                       result=off (expected off)
PASS | Claude Sonnet 4.6 + global=adaptive                     result=adaptive (expected adaptive)
PASS | Claude Sonnet 4.6 + global=low                          result=low (expected low)
PASS | Claude Opus 4.7 + global=adaptive                       result=off (expected off)
PASS | Claude Opus 4.8 + global=adaptive                       result=off (expected off)
PASS | Ollama + per-model params=low + global=adaptive         result=low (expected low)
PASS | Ollama + per-model params=off + global=low              result=off (expected off)
========================================
10 passed, 0 failed
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Ollama + global `thinkingDefault: "low"` → `"off"` (provider default wins)
  2. Ollama + global `thinkingDefault: "adaptive"` → `"off"` (provider default wins)
  3. Ollama + per-model `params.thinking: "low"` → `"low"` (per-model override works)
  4. Ollama + per-model `params.thinking: "off"` → `"off"` (per-model override works)
  5. Unknown provider + global `thinkingDefault: "low"` → `"low"` (no provider default, global applies)
  6. Claude Opus 4.7 + global `thinkingDefault: "adaptive"` → `"off"` (hardcoded special case preserved)
  7. No global default → returns provider default

- What was not tested: Real Ollama end-to-end with actual model inference (requires local Ollama instance with a thinking-capable model). The fix is in a pure function whose behavior is fully covered by real runtime invocation with 10/10 scenarios passing.
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**
  - ✅ Auth guard: No policy/permission change
  - ✅ Enum completeness: All thinking levels (`off`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`adaptive`/etc.) handled by existing checks; the fix only reorders them
  - ✅ Path coverage: Single change in shared `resolveThinkingDefault()` covers cron, embedded runner (session), and subagent paths
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: No new state to clean up

## Root Cause

In `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts`, `resolveThinkingDefault()` checked `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` (lines 71-73) **before** `resolveThinkingDefaultForModel()` (lines 101-106), so the global config default unconditionally overrode the provider-specific default from plugin policy or catalog metadata.

Introduced by: Peter Steinberger (`steipete`) in commit `d5eec80e340` — the initial implementation of `resolveThinkingDefault()`.

## Regression Test Plan

All 9 new unit tests pass on every run. Existing `thinking-runtime.test.ts` (8 tests) continues to pass — no behavioral change for Claude models or unconfigured providers.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Ollama users who have `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` set will no longer see forced thinking mode in cron agentTurn jobs. The Ollama model will run with its default behavior (thinking off) unless explicitly configured per-model via `agents.defaults.models[].params.thinking`.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: All code paths through `resolveThinkingDefault()` — per-model override, Claude special cases, Ollama default with global config, unknown provider with global config, no global config
- Edge cases checked: Global `thinkingDefault: "off"` with provider that also defaults to "off" (result is "off" either way); global `thinkingDefault: "adaptive"` for unknown provider with reasoning model
- What you did NOT verify: Real Ollama E2E without a local Ollama instance

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — the only behavioral change is that providers with `defaultLevel: "off"` are no longer overridden by the global default, which is a bug fix
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The shared layer (`resolveThinkingDefault()`) is the correct boundary because all code paths (cron, session, subagent) depend on it. A cron-only fix would have been ineffective because the embedded runner independently resolves defaults.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Removing the `resolveThinkingDefault()` call from the cron path only — rejected because the embedded runner (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts:291-314`) independently resolves defaults via the same function, so the bug would reappear for non-cron paths

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: The fix was designed after reading the full call chain from `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts` through `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` to `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts`, confirming that a shared-layer fix was needed rather than the cron-only approach originally suggested in the issue

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Users who intentionally set `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` and expect it to apply globally to all providers including Ollama.

**Mitigation**: These users can still enable thinking per-model via `agents.defaults.models["ollama/..."].params.thinking`, which takes highest priority. The previous behavior was a bug (forcing thinking on models that explicitly default to "off"), not a documented feature.

**No known breaking changes** for Claude or other providers without an explicit plugin default, as `resolveThinkingDefaultForModel()` returns a generic fallback (`"medium"` for reasoning models) that is not `"off"`, so the global default continues to apply.

---

Fixes #104212

target.title: fix(gateway): cap history when numeric limit is huge
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users requesting Gateway HTTP session history with an all-digit `limit` value above JavaScript's safe integer range would receive the minimum one-message page instead of the endpoint's bounded maximum history window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct REST history query parser now keeps non-digit limits on the existing minimum fallback while capping all-digit values that exceed safe integer parsing to the existing `MAX_SESSION_HISTORY_LIMIT`. This stays inside the Gateway HTTP history boundary and does not change cursor pagination, SSE streaming, RPC schemas, or configuration.

## User Impact

Gateway HTTP history callers that pass a very large numeric limit get a bounded useful page instead of unexpectedly truncating the response to one message.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: direct REST `/sessions/:sessionKey/history` caps an all-digit limit above the safe integer range to the endpoint's bounded maximum instead of treating it as `1`.
- Current head: `d27121efce282d386fb73f04e7c2be9a5e2add02`.
- Direct Gateway HTTP proof: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` started `src/gateway/server.ts`, seeded a file-backed session transcript with three assistant messages, and fetched the production `GET /sessions/:sessionKey/history` HTTP route with a 100-digit `limit`.

```json
{
  "head": "d27121efce282d386fb73f04e7c2be9a5e2add02",
  "proofPath": "production src/gateway/server.ts -> GET /sessions/:sessionKey/history",
  "request": {
    "method": "GET",
    "path": "/sessions/agent%3Amain%3Amain/history?limit=9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999",
    "header": "x-openclaw-scopes: operator.read"
  },
  "response": {
    "status": 200,
    "sessionKey": "agent:main:main",
    "messageCount": 3,
    "texts": [
      "first message",
      "second message",
      "third message"
    ],
    "hasMore": false,
    "nextCursorPresent": false
  }
}
```

- Formatting: `node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.CMD --check --threads=1 src\gateway\sessions-history-http.ts src\gateway\sessions-history-http.test.ts` passed.

- Observed result: the 100-digit `limit` query returned all three seeded history messages with `hasMore: false` and no cursor, instead of falling back to a one-message page.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the Gateway HTTP history parser, direct HTTP proof, and regression test and understand the bounded limit fix.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): use truncateUtf16Safe for web snapshot maxChars cap
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `qaWebSnapshot` can produce invalid Unicode when a page's body text contains emoji or other supplementary-plane characters near the `maxChars` truncation boundary.

`qaWebSnapshot` caps the body text returned to QA scenarios with `text.slice(0, maxChars)`. QA scenarios use `maxChars: 12000` to snapshot the OpenClaw control UI, which can contain agent messages with emoji. When the page text reaches the cap with an emoji at the boundary, `slice` leaves a lone high surrogate in `snapshot.text` — which is then passed through `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` and used in `text.includes(needle)` assertions, potentially causing spurious needle misses.

**Concrete example:** `text = "abc🤖end"` (🤖 = U+1F916, two code units) with `maxChars: 4` — raw `.slice(0, 4)` keeps `"abc" + U+D83E`, a lone high surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `text.slice(0, maxChars)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, matching the established pattern used across `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts`, and others. No behavioral change when `maxChars` is unset or the text fits within the cap.

## User Impact

**Before:** QA scenarios that call `webSnapshot({ maxChars: 12000, … })` on a page whose text hits the cap with an emoji at the boundary receive `snapshot.text` with a lone surrogate, which can silently corrupt needle searches and produce unexpected scan misses.

**After:** `snapshot.text` is always well-formed Unicode; boundary emoji are dropped whole instead of split.

## Evidence

- `extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.ts` — `qaWebSnapshot` uses `truncateUtf16Safe` for the head cap
- `qa/scenarios/ui/control-ui-qa-channel-image-roundtrip.yaml` — live QA scenario using `webSnapshot({ maxChars: 12000, … })` with emoji needle checks as canonical reachability
- `src/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime.ts` — exports `truncateUtf16Safe` as a proper SDK subpath for bundled plugins
- Regression: `extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts` — new `does not split a surrogate pair when truncating snapshot text at maxChars` case

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `qaWebSnapshot` with an active `maxChars` cap no longer leaves unpaired UTF-16 surrogates when page body text contains emoji at the truncation boundary.
- **Canonical reachability path:** QA scenario `webSnapshot({ pageId, maxChars: 12000, … })` → `qaWebSnapshot` → `body.textContent()` → `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)` → `snapshot.text` → `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(snapshot.text).includes(needle)` in scenario assertion.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; no real browser needed — `bodyLocator.textContent` mock in the colocated Vitest injects the surrogate-boundary input directly into the production `qaWebSnapshot` code path.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `truncateUtf16Safe` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`; no provider/channel constraints — this is plugin-local web snapshot text handling.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin 24.3.0), Node v22, branch `fix/qa-lab-web-snapshot-utf16`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
# 1. Real Chromium integration proof (playwright-core, headless)
$ cat playwright-utf16-proof.mts   # proof script (runs from repo root)
# launches real Chromium via playwright-core, calls page.setContent() with
# emoji content, reads body.textContent(), then shows raw .slice vs truncateUtf16Safe
$ pnpm exec tsx playwright-utf16-proof.mts

# 2. Regression suite
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx playwright-utf16-proof.mts
=== real Chromium body.textContent() proof ===
body.textContent() length (code units): 8 | value: "abc🤖end"

raw .slice(0, 4):
  length: 4
  unpaired_surrogates: true
  hex: U+0061 U+0062 U+0063 U+D83E

truncateUtf16Safe(text, 4):
  length: 3
  unpaired_surrogates: false
  value: "abc"

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 RUN  v4.1.9 /Users/shen/Documents/GitHub/openclaw

 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > opens, interacts with, snapshots, and closes a page 78ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > launches an explicit Chromium executable override when configured 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > launches detected system Chromium without requiring branded Chrome 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > keeps an explicit browser channel request explicit 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > can close only selected page sessions 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > does not split a surrogate pair when truncating snapshot text at maxChars 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > caps oversized web runtime timeouts 1ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
   Start at  15:22:37
   Duration  535ms (transform 475ms, setup 321ms, import 44ms, tests 83ms, environment 0ms)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Real headless Chromium (playwright-core, Chrome Headless Shell 149) loads `"abc🤖end"` via `page.setContent()` and `body.textContent()` returns an 8-code-unit JS string. Raw `.slice(0, 4)` leaves `U+D83E` alone (`unpaired_surrogates: true`). `truncateUtf16Safe(text, 4)` returns `"abc"` (`unpaired_surrogates: false`). This is the same real Playwright `locator("body").textContent()` call path that `qaWebSnapshot` uses. Regression suite: 7/7 pass including the new surrogate-boundary test. The only failing CI shard (`src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`) is pre-existing on `upstream/main` — reproduced locally without this patch.
- **What was not tested:** Full live QA E2E scenario (`control-ui-qa-channel-image-roundtrip`) with a real OpenClaw gateway rendering 12,000+ code units of agent output with emoji at the boundary. The Playwright `body.textContent()` → `truncateUtf16Safe` path is fully verified above.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
- Single commit on `upstream/main`; no bundled `scripts/` or release-script changes
